# SpeckLock — consolidated pre-release inventory

**Verification note.** The six recon reports were written against an older tree. Since then the README has been substantially hardened (Round 8 landed, a training-data leak was disclosed, the oracle sensor and the 0/3 counter-run were added to the results table). Several findings they marked "blocker" are **already fixed in README.md and nowhere else**. That fact is itself the headline problem below. Every claim I repeat here I opened and checked; anything I could not confirm is marked UNVERIFIED.

---

## (a) Must be FIXED before release

### 1. The public site publishes what the README already retracted — VERIFIED, and this is the launch risk

This is the single most damaging item, because `docs/index.html` is the thing a LinkedIn post links to, and the repo now contains its own refutation.

`README.md:41` says the 1.000 result is **"not 'unseen'... That is a development set"**. `docs/index.html:7` (meta description) and `:9` (og:description — this is the social card text) still say **"AP/F1 1.000 on unseen real video; 24/24 intercepted"**.

`README.md:44` states the old ARD-MAV 0.994 row is superseded, and `README.md:129+` carries a banner: *"The ARD-MAV column of the last row is void... `combined_splits()` ignored the published 15-video test list and re-split by position, so rounds 5–7 trained on most of the official test set."* `docs/index.html:422` still publishes **0.994 / 0.801** as a live results table with no banner.

`README.md:47` now discloses the oracle and `README.md:48` adds the honest counterpart row (0/3, detection rate 4.4%). On the site: `grep -c oracle docs/index.html` = **1**, and that single hit is at `:795` inside a copy-paste command block, not a disclosure. The hero stat `:246` and results table `:484` print "24 / 24" bare.

`docs/gallery.html`: `grep -c oracle` = **0**. Ten city cards (`:96`–`:105`) each print "detection rate 0.97 / 0.88 / 0.98". I confirmed `work/pursuit/city_clips/results.json` has `detector: "oracle"`, n=10, hits=10. Six chase cards (`:110`–`:115`) use the *identical* label for runs that did have a real detector. The generator cannot currently tell them apart — `docs/media/showcase.json` has a `detect_rate` field and **no `detector` field at all** (verified). Meanwhile the same city mission with a real detector scores 0.022–0.044 (`work/pursuit/city_pipe/results.json`), so the advertised 0.88 is ~20–40× the real-sensor rate for the same scenario.

**Fix:** propagate the README's results table wholesale into `docs/index.html` and add a `detector` field to `showcase.json` + a qualifier in `tools/make_gallery.py:179`. Do not launch until the og/meta strings match the README.

### 2. A fabricated latency figure is still live, and it argues the opposite of the finding — VERIFIED

`pursuit/README.md:382` records the retraction in the repo's own words: an earlier *"53.9 ms, 18.5 FPS"* **"was a hardcoded literal in `pursuit/tools/city_report.py` with no run behind it."**

`docs/index.html:750` still asserts perception went "to 53.9 ms" and concludes **"the detector is 100% of the reason... The remaining gap to a 50 ms budget is a pure inference problem."** The corrected figure — 231.5 ms — is printed on the *same page* at `:655`. And `pursuit/README.md:389` states the actual breakdown inverts the conclusion: *"on the ring the network is 7% of the loop and the answer is the motion stage."* The site tells the reader to optimise the wrong stage using a number the repo says was invented.

### 3. The test count is wrong in four places — VERIFIED by running it

I ran `python -m pytest --collect-only -q`: **772 tests collected**.

- `README.md:46` — "**540** unit tests" next to the exact command `python -m pytest`
- `README.md:252` — "# 540 tests in ~22 s"
- `docs/research/INFRA.md:96` — "**Expect `807 passed`**... `dronedet/tests` contributes 267"
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml:31` — "797 collected = 540 pursuit + 257 dronedet"

Actual `dronedet/tests` is **232** — lower than both 267 and 257, so those component counts were never right. `README.md:293` and `pursuit/README.md:24` say 540 for `pursuit/` alone, which *is* correct; the error is only where 540 is presented as the whole suite. CI cannot catch it: `MIN_TOTAL` is 600 (`tests.yml:35`). This is the cheapest possible thing for a reviewer to falsify — one command — which is exactly why it damages credibility out of proportion to its size.

### 4. README contradicts itself on the generalist result — VERIFIED, three different numbers

For one claim ("one model, all datasets"), `README.md` publishes:
- `:44` — ARD-MAV **0.809** (Round 8, official 15-video split, 3 seeds)
- `:107` — ARD-MAV **0.994**, NPS **0.801**
- `:128` — **0.84** ARD-MAV · 0.81 NPS

`:107` is the per-clip number: `tools/eval_improvements.py:32-35` hardcodes exactly one clip per dataset (`phantom16`, `Clip_19`, `10_06`), and `docs/reports/round7-fusion.md:50` is explicitly a per-clip table. `:128` is the pooled split from `round5:53`. Worse, `:107` sits *above* the leak banner that voids it, with no marker. `phantom16`'s median target is 39.1 px — 3.5× the dataset median — so the headlined clip does not test the few-pixel thesis at all.

**Fix:** delete `:107`'s numbers or mark them void inline; keep only the Round 8 official-split figures as headline.

### 5. Two contradictory values for one deterministic run — VERIFIED

`--suite full --latency-frames 3 [--compensate-latency]`:
- **32/42 vs 18/42** — `README.md:333`, `pursuit/README.md:698,702,927,975`
- **36/42 vs 17/42** — `docs/index.html:756`, `pursuit/guidance.py:795`

`pursuit/README.md:703` asserts *"deterministic, so both numbers reproduce exactly"* — which is precisely the guarantee two published pairs break. `docs/research/internal-audit-2026-08.md:52` records a re-run yielding 32/42 and 18/42, i.e. the site and the docstring hold the wrong pair. I could not re-run the suite myself, so **which pair is correct is UNVERIFIED by me** — but that they disagree is verified, and one of them must go.

### 6. "These are the causal numbers" is false for the shipped runner — VERIFIED

`README.md:85` heads the shipped-models table: *"These are the **causal** numbers, frame by frame with no look-ahead."* `final/run_final.py:111` passes `"--smooth-coast"`. `docs/reports/round3-deliverables.md:122` defines coast smoothing as up to **60 frames of look-ahead**, *"only legal for a recorded-and-reviewed surveillance product"*, and `:196` says so explicitly: *"the shipped package's headline tracked metric is the offline surveillance-mode number."* The 10_06 value is unaffected (both modes give 1.000), but the header claim is wrong as written, and the 07_05 column is from the split-trained generation, not the shipped weights.

### 7. Unsourced numbers in the SOTA comparison table — VERIFIED

`README.md:123` / `docs/index.html:450`: **"Dogfight | NPS | 0.89 | 0.50 on ARD100"**. I grepped the tree: no Dogfight ARD100 score exists anywhere. The ARD100 numbers the repo holds (`docs/references/few-pixel-drone-methods-survey.md:146-151`) are YOLOMG 0.85/0.78, YOLOv5/v8 baseline **0.53**, YOLOv9 0.64, TransVisDrone 0.15 — none is Dogfight. `docs/research/datasets-and-benchmarks-2026.md:360` says outright: *"Treat Dogfight as an annotation source and a citation, never as something you ran."*

`arXiv 2504.11967` — cited at `README.md:112` and `docs/index.html:443` as the authority for "no unified multi-dataset model", the load-bearing premise for the contribution claim. It appears in exactly three files: those two, plus `internal-audit-2026-08.md` flagging this very gap. It is absent from all of `docs/references/`. A claim of the form "no published method does X" resting on a reference the repo does not hold is the weakest link in the whole document set.

Also: the table mixes datasets (competitors' collapse measured on **ARD100**, ours on **ARD-MAV**) and the bolded TransVisDrone 0.15 is a competitor's reimplementation that `few-pixel-drone-methods-survey.md:180` says to "treat cautiously".

### 8. Two third-party checkpoints redistributed without attribution — VERIFIED

`NOTICE.md` has a meticulous third-party table but covers neither:
- `baseline/yolo26n-new-data_full__2026_Jan_19.pt` (5.6 MB, present). `NOTICE.md:21` names `yolo26n` under the Ultralytics AGPL row — that covers the *architecture licence*, not who trained this checkpoint or on what data. `docs/guides/methods.md:165` calls it an "external baseline"; the filename reads like someone else's training run.
- `work/models/FSRCNN_x4.pb` (41 KB, present) — pretrained OpenCV `dnn_superres` weights, **absent from NOTICE.md entirely**.

For an AGPL public release, settle this before going public, not after.

## (b) Must be MEASURED — currently asserted

### dt = 6 is the project's founding constant and has essentially no evidence

The entire justification is one prose row: `docs/reports/round3-deliverables.md:162` (DT=9 rejected, val 0.710 vs 0.719). No detection JSON, no checkpoint, no seed, no CI backs it — and `round3:169` states the training runs were discarded, so it cannot be re-derived. Neighbouring rows in the same table (INT8, full-frame stabiliser) *do* have artifacts under `realtime/work/out3/`, which makes the gap conspicuous.

There is no single source of truth. I verified five independent hardcoded sites: `tools/make_datasets_v3.py:49`, `tools/make_dataset_ft7.py:31`, `realtime/tools/make_datasets_rt.py:30`, `realtime/pipelines.py:59` (shipped EDGE-RT inference), `dronedet/methods/hybrid2.py:32` (shipped PC-MAX, comment: *"must match make_dataset_ft7"*). A parallel family runs at **DT = 3**: `tools/make_temporal_combined.py:20`, `tools/make_fusion_combined.py:35`. Only `make_datasets_v3.py` has a `--dt` override, and the two shipped inference paths cannot be changed without editing source — so an inference-side dt sweep is impossible as written.

Worse: **the one registered temporal ablation uses `stack_dt=3`** (`configs/experiments/temporal.py:74`), so the experiment defending the founding claim validates a tap spacing no shipped model uses. And `stack_dt` is declarative only — nothing reads it; it lands in `MANIFEST.json` and that is all.

**This is the measurement I would prioritise.** "Three moments at t−12/t−6/t" is the thesis of the whole project and of the LinkedIn post. Right now it rests on one unreproducible row.

### The experiment registry has never been run

8 configs, 5 groups, import-time validation, VRAM anchors, provenance manifests — genuinely good infrastructure. `find . -name RESULT.json` returns nothing; `work/runs/*/MANIFEST.json` does not exist; `work/scorecards/` does not exist. The paired-bootstrap / Holm / McNemar machinery in `dronedet/stats.py` and `tools/compare.py`, built specifically to make ablations defensible, has never been fed an input.

Separately: **no nano/edge variant is registered at all**. All 8 configs are `yolov8s-p2` at imgsz 640. The flagship real-time deliverable is the one model the reproducibility infrastructure does not cover.

### `work/ablation/REPORT.md` Experiment 1 is not a controlled ablation

Verified at `tools/ablation_temporal.py:47-56`: the "single-frame" arm is `tools/run_baseline.py --weights baseline/yolo26n-*.pt`; the "temporal" arm is `final/run_final.py --profile edge-rt`. Different architecture, different training corpus, different resolution — presented under a column headed **"input representation"** (`REPORT.md:9`) reporting 0.110 vs 1.000. Only the resolution difference is disclosed (`REPORT.md:7`). The weights-and-corpus difference is never mentioned, and Experiment 2 in the same file goes out of its way to state exactly this class of caveat.

A properly controlled pair already exists on disk and is not what the script scores: `rt-c-full1280` vs `rt-f-single1280` — same net family, same corpus, same 1280 px, same pipeline — **0.894 vs 0.188** on 10_06, with committed JSONs under `realtime/work/out/{0705,1006}/rt-f-single1280/`. Score that instead. The real result is nearly as strong and is defensible.

Also, `REPORT.md:12` prints a 95% CI of **[1.000, 1.000]** on n = 1 video / 1 drone, without the qualifier `dronedet/stats.py:26-33` insists on for exactly this case.

### Constants asserted without evidence

Not blockers, but a reviewer will ask. `dronedet/motion.py:27-45` — 18 constants in one constructor; only `lag` has a measurement. `dronedet/trackclass.py:28-36` — 6 constants, and the docstring at `:5` admits they were fitted on 10_06, the test video (the README now correctly labels 10_06 a development set as a result). `dronedet/track.py:27-58` — 18 more; only the association floor was swept, and it now exists in three places with two values (0.25 at `dronedet/track.py:148,297` and `dronedet/cli.py:175`; 0.2 at `realtime/runner.py:24`). Stabilisation on/off is one flag away (`dronedet/cli.py:136`) and has never been run. τ = 12.0 (`dronedet/evaluate.py:62`) has no sensitivity curve. NWD blends 0.5/0.5 (`configs/experiments/base.py:145`) are pure defaults.

### EDGE-RT has never run on an edge device

`docs/research/INFRA.md:712` states it plainly. Every Jetson number in `realtime/README.md:62-80` is a projection, correctly labelled there — but the framing "edge model" invites the inference. The only genuine Jetson Orin Nano measurement in the repo belongs to someone else's method.

## (c) Fine — do not spend time here

**The edge model exists and is real.** VERIFIED. `final/edge_rt/edge_n1280.pt` (6.6 MB) plus portable `.onnx` and `.fp16.onnx`. Architecture at `realtime/pipelines.py:203-231`: one YOLOv8n-P2 on the 3-frame stabilised stack, full-frame @1280, no tiling, no proposal stage, no expert. The `.gitignore` deliberately re-includes `!final/edge_rt/*.onnx` so it stays portable.

**The "100+ FPS" model is not a separate model — and I proved it.** I unzipped the `.pt` archives and hashed only the tensor storage blobs:

```
full_temporal_n1280.pt   441 tensors  6,357,242 bytes  75c9b80997c49cfeff0d
full_temporal_n640.pt    441 tensors  6,357,242 bytes  75c9b80997c49cfeff0d   ← identical
edge_n1280.pt            441 tensors  6,357,242 bytes  c0737feeae250763261e
v3_full_temporal_n1280.pt 441 tensors 6,357,242 bytes  6a561d20835891bd5fce
```

rt-d @640 is the same weights at half resolution, exported twice (`realtime/tools/run_round3.py:35-39` `shutil.copy`s one `best.pt` to both stems). The 104 fps costs a lot: 10_06 AP 0.894 → 0.631, and on 07_05 it collapses to 0.243. **Describe it as "the same net at half resolution, at a third less AP" — never as a separate edge model.** The repo already treats it as a rejected operating point, correctly.

**`tools/check_docs.py` passes.** A recon report claimed three false failures from missing `encoding=` on a cp1255 locale. I ran it: exit 0, *"checked 61 documents — all links resolve and are tracked"*, with and without `PYTHONUTF8=1`. **That finding does not reproduce.** The broader missing-`encoding=` pattern in report *writers* (`tools/compare.py:332`, `tools/ablation_temporal.py:193`, `pursuit/tools/*.py`) is real and worth a cleanup pass, but it is cosmetic, not release-blocking.

**Hygiene is genuinely clean.** Zero secrets/tokens/credentials. Zero TODO/FIXME/HACK. No debugger hooks, no commented-out code, no merge markers, no editor cruft. No large blob in git history that isn't still in HEAD — no history rewrite needed. The apparent "duplicate script families" (`make_dataset*.py` ×8, `final_round{,2,3}.py`) are a deliberate chronological research trail, each docstring naming its round. Do not delete any of it.

**Do not "fix" `configs/yolov8m-p2-ch4.yaml`** being byte-identical to the `s` variant — that is correct Ultralytics convention; the scale comes from the filename.

**Keep `docs/research/internal-audit-2026-08.md` public.** It is a credibility asset. But add a dated "resolved since" column — it currently reads as a live list of open defects, several of which the README has since fixed, and at least one (the gallery) it has not.

**The README results table (`:39`–`:50`) is now genuinely good** — every row carries its n and its sensor, and disputed rows link to their corrections. That is the standard. The job is to make `docs/index.html` and `docs/gallery.html` meet it.

## The blunt version

The research is careful and the round reports are disciplined. Every serious problem is a **propagation failure**, and every omission runs in the flattering direction. You have already done the hard, honest work in `README.md`; the public site is a stale snapshot of the version you retracted. If a reviewer opens the GitHub Pages site and then the README, they will find the contradiction in under two minutes, and the charitable reading — "he fixed it and forgot the site" — is not the one a hostile reader will pick.

Two things gate a launch: **sync `docs/index.html` + `docs/gallery.html` to the README**, and **fix the test count**. Everything in (b) can ship as stated open questions — a "what I haven't measured yet" section is a strength, not a liability, provided dt=6 is named there honestly rather than defended with a number that cannot be reproduced.
